children: China's export strength has proven to be a "double-edged sword" for China's economy, according to BofA Securities in a research note. "On the one hand, robust external demand has provided a critical buffer against weak domestic demand, helping keep overall growth on track to meet the lower bound of the government's 4.5% growth target," the bank says. However, persistently strong export performance, has reduced the urgency for policymakers to deliver additional easing measures, BofA says. Policymakers has refrained from announcing fresh stimulus at the July Politburo meeting, opting instead to emphasize more effective implementation of existing policies, they say. (tracy.qu@wsj.com)
